_comment: Tier-2 for fourc::fs3i#6, and a FALSIFICATION of its advice. The entry said 'Set TIMESTEP equal in both fields' and predicted a 5-15% drift otherwise. Upstream fs3i_part_1wc_infperm.4C.yaml is a passing 4C regression case that deliberately does the opposite: FS3I DYNAMIC TIMESTEP 12.5 against FSI DYNAMIC and SCALAR TRANSPORT DYNAMIC TIMESTEP 25, i.e. the outer coupling step is half the field step. Setting the FS3I step to 25 so all three agree does not drift — it fails outright with 'Core::LinearSolver::BelosSolver: Iterative solver did not converge.' from core/linear_solver/src/method/4C_linear_solver_method_iterative.cpp line 193, producing no result lines at all (EQUAL_RESULT_LINES=0), so there is no percentage to compare. Verified by execution 2026-08-06 against 4C at /home/alexander/4C/build/4C (2026.2.0-dev, commit 89519cfe76).
expect_in_output: Core::LinearSolver::BelosSolver: Iterative solver did not converge.

_mutation.note: remove the pathology: leave the FS3I coupling step at the upstream 12.5, half the field step. EQUAL_ARM_STEPS_MATCH flips to 'no' (a forbidden token), the Belos non-convergence vanishes and the fixture must go red.
